rejected_representation.text: The soundness and completeness proof for the 248-coordinate baseline is established in Section~\ref{v15:base248}. The scalar-S argument in Section~\ref{v15:reductions} changes its nonzero integer index to $|a|$ and preserves both directions. The three subsequent coordinate changes and the displayed affine and row operations are rational witness bijections, with the only nonconstant inverse powers justified by $R>0$. Their composition therefore proves the defining equivalence in Theorem~\ref{thm:v15-main}. The same sufficiently large $N_0$ works for all larger $N$: the fixed aggregate bound first excludes the nonzero defect, and $149^{-L_N}\to0$ then gives the Lucas contradiction uniformly. The explicit equations below specify the resulting family. Their integer square expansion has coefficient one on $z_1^4$, degree four, and the stated coefficient profile; this last step is finite integer arithmetic and is independently reproducible from the complete displayed system. In particular it does not make $N_0$ effective.
